summary: Issue #184 T5 peak-RSS observation. Read-only scale anchor: C:\Users\akiyoshi\.config\cheaper\usage.jsonl, 823 lines, 257336 bytes, 197 kind=run and 626 kind=count, no route/refetch records; contents were not copied. Since this real log is small and has no route mix, generated a synthetic bounded fallback at %TEMP%\cheaper-usage-t5-issue-184\config\usage.jsonl: 82300 records (100x observed line count), 29892700 bytes, SHA256 F3B09EB8702A6153449C5A9F951CC26E67DA690F4CB6AF65C2ACB6100E897B02; 61725 run / 16460 route / 4115 route-refetch (75/20/5 assumed mix). Recipe: for i=0..82299 use i%20; phases 0..14 emit synthetic run records, phases 15..18 emit route records with route-{i%8} and logRef log-{i}, phase 19 emits route-refetch with logRef log-{i-1}; all timestamps are 2026-10-26T00:00:00.000Z and values are fixed synthetic numbers. The route mix and 100x scale are fallback assumptions, not observed production proportions. Command: launch target/debug/cheaper.exe usage --group-by route with CHEAPER_CONFIG_DIR pointing at the fixture config directory; PowerShell System.Diagnostics.ProcessStartInfo redirects stdout/stderr, reads them asynchronously, samples Process.PeakWorkingSet64 every 5 ms until exit, then records PeakWorkingSet64 and elapsed time. Repeated twice on the same fixture/hash: exit 0, 363565056 bytes (346.72 MiB), 2927 ms; 363585536 bytes (346.74 MiB), 2894 ms. Environment: Windows 11 Pro x64 10.0.26200; rustc 1.99.0 (b940084d7 2026-09-28), cargo 1.99.0. Decision: retain Vec<Value> and keep streaming deferred; there is no approved memory pass/fail threshold, so this measurement establishes a reproducible baseline only and does not claim a threshold pass. Revisit design when usage-log growth or an explicit memory budget supplies a trigger. Stored under docs/impl/exp because benchmarks/results is reserved for cheaper-bench schemaVersion 2 artifacts.

Reproducibility check on the event's same fixture: command was `target/debug/cheaper.exe usage --group-by route`, with CHEAPER_CONFIG_DIR set to the fixture config directory; parent PowerShell used System.Diagnostics.ProcessStartInfo with stdout/stderr redirected and drained asynchronously, sampled child PeakWorkingSet64 every 5 ms, then read final PeakWorkingSet64/exit code/elapsed time. A copyable launch setup is: `$psi=[System.Diagnostics.ProcessStartInfo]::new(); $psi.FileName=(Resolve-Path 'target/debug/cheaper.exe').Path; $psi.WorkingDirectory=(Get-Location).Path; foreach($a in @('usage','--group-by','route')){$psi.ArgumentList.Add($a)}; $psi.Environment['CHEAPER_CONFIG_DIR']=$configDir; $psi.RedirectStandardOutput=$true; $psi.RedirectStandardError=$true; $psi.UseShellExecute=$false`. Same fixture SHA256 F3B09EB8702A6153449C5A9F951CC26E67DA690F4CB6AF65C2ACB6100E897B02, 29892700 bytes, 82300 records. Third result: exit 0, PeakWorkingSet64=363737088 bytes (346.89 MiB), 2920 ms. Across three runs peak RSS was 346.72-346.89 MiB; exact fixture dimensions/hash were unchanged. This is reproducibility evidence, not a threshold verdict.
